data.title: Evidence for direct activation of mTORC2 kinase activity by phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate
data.authors: Gan X; Wu D et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: PIP3 directly stimulates mTORC2 kinase activity, linking PI3K to mTORC2.
data.abstract_excerpt: mTORC2 (mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2) plays important roles in signal transduction by regulating an array of downstream effectors, including protein kinase AKT. However, its regulation by upstream regulators remains poorly characterized. Although phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate (PtdIns(3,4,5)P(3)) is known to regulate the phosphorylation of AKT Ser(473), the hydrophobic motif (HM) site, by mTORC2, it is not clear whether PtdIns(3,4,5)P(3) can directly regulate mTORC2 kinase activity.

extracted_findings.effect: PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 (PIP3) directly activates mTORC2 kinase activity toward Akt Ser473
